title: LexGenius: An Expert-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Legal General Intelligence

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent); the paper gives only the undated alias 'GPT-4.1 nano' (equals gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14)

task.subset_rule: all (8,385 MCQs in the 20 Ability_*.json files); each item asked twice with the answer options shuffled (Sec. 5.1) and the two scores averaged
task.approximation: our own two seeded shuffles (seed 20260907 + item index); the way the Naive instruction and the question/options are joined is not printed; single pass in the released option order (the runner has no seeded option shuffle; the paper averages two shuffled passes)

items.source: QwenQKing/LexGenius (Hub parquet conversion of the 20 Ability_*.json files; the files hold 8,345 MCQs in total, not 8,385)

prompt.source_location: Appendix D.2, Figure 29 (Naive Prompt, original Chinese text); English translation printed alongside
prompt.verbatim: partial (instruction verbatim; placement of the question and options after the instruction assumed)

placeholders_prose.question: items.question
placeholders_prose.options: the four option texts re-lettered A.-D. after the seeded shuffle, one per line

output.postprocess: strip; compare with the shuffled position of the gold answer; unparsable counts as incorrect
output.parse_prose: letter (A-D): first standalone letter A-D in the reply

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of correct answers over the 8,385 MCQs, in percent, averaged over the two option shuffles
metric.original_location: Table 2, row GPT-4.1 nano, column Overall Nai. (CoT: 54.62)

notes: 8,385 x 2 shuffles x 3 seeds calls at ~$0.0005 each. Per-dimension columns of Table 2 allow finer checks; the Ability_*.json files also give the 20-ability breakdown of Table 7 (LLM 12). Options are stored already prefixed 'A.'-'D.', so they are joined with newlines rather than re-lettered.
